title: Hot Face Emoji 🥵 Meaning: Heat, Spice and Attraction
description: 🥵 is red, sweating and panting. It means sweltering weather, a brutal workout, fiery food or finding someone extremely attractive. Here is how to read it.
summary: The 🥵 hot face means overheated. People use it for scorching weather, exhausting exercise and food that is too spicy. Just as often it means someone is physically attractive, hot in the slang sense, and the sender is flustered by it. Context tells you whether the heat is literal or flirtatious.
meaning: A bright red face with its tongue hanging out and sweat running down is not a subtle image. In the literal sense 🥵 describes a body that cannot cool down: a heat wave, a subway car with broken air conditioning, the last mile of a run, a sauna. It is a complaint, usually a lighthearted one, about temperature or effort.

Spicy food is the second literal use. Hot wings, chili challenges and curries ordered one level too brave all earn 🥵, often with a pepper or fire next to it. The panting tongue fits the experience precisely, and food creators use it to flag heat levels in captions or to show that a dish defeated them.

The slang meaning comes from the word hot. Sent in reply to a photo or video of a person, 🥵 says they look so good the sender is sweating. It is openly lustful, a step beyond the fire emoji, and it is one of the main thirst emojis on social media. People use it for celebrities, partners and crushes, and sometimes ironically for a friend's unflattering picture.

Because both meanings are so common, misreadings are rare but possible. A message that says the gym was 🥵 is about exertion; a 🥵 under a gym selfie is about the person. When there is real doubt, the flirtatious reading is the one most people now reach for first, so it pays to add a word or two.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Weather and workouts account for many everyday uses, as in it is 98 degrees out 🥵. Between partners or people flirting, it is a reaction to a photo or a suggestive comment and signals attraction. If a friend sends it about your new haircut, take it as an enthusiastic compliment.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Thirst comments are its natural habitat. Under videos of actors, athletes, musicians and influencers, 🥵 appears in rows, often with 🔥 or 😮‍💨. Fitness and cooking accounts use it literally for tough sessions and spicy recipes, so the same emoji serves two very different crowds.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: This is a clear signal. A person who replies 🥵 to your picture is saying they find you physically attractive, more forcefully than a heart-eyes face would. It is not a declaration of feelings, only of attraction, and it is meant to be noticed.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Keep it to literal heat, such as a broken office thermostat or an outdoor event in July, and even then use it sparingly. Because the flirtatious sense is so well known, applying it to anything involving a colleague's appearance is inappropriate and could be reported.

examples.meaning: The sender is uncomfortably hot because of the weather.
A workout left them sweaty and exhausted.

examples.meaning: Out of breath and overheated from climbing stairs.

combos.meaning: Extremely attractive, or extremely hot in temperature; the fire intensifies either reading.
Food that is too spicy to handle comfortably.
Suffering through a heat wave or a blazing summer day.
Dripping with sweat after exercise, though it can read as suggestive.

confusedWith.difference: 🤒 is the emoji for a fever and illness. 🥵 is hot from outside causes like sun, effort or spice, or from attraction. Sending 🥵 to say you are sick may be read as flirting.
🫠 dissolves into a puddle and mostly conveys embarrassment, dread or sarcastic resignation, though it works for heat too. 🥵 stays solid, red and panting, and has the thirsty meaning that 🫠 lacks.
🤤 expresses wanting something, including food. 🥵 expresses being overwhelmed by heat or by how good someone looks. For a plate of pasta use 🤤; for the chef, people use 🥵.

avoid: Do not send it about a coworker, a student or anyone in a professional relationship with you.
Avoid it under photos of minors or of strangers who did not invite comments on their looks.
Be careful using it for real heat exhaustion or fever when you need to be taken seriously.
design: A red or deep orange-red face with furrowed, strained eyebrows, its tongue hanging from an open mouth and beads of sweat on the forehead or cheeks. Platforms agree on these elements. The number and position of sweat drops differ, and some designs shade the face darker at the top, like a rising flush.

faqs.q: What does 🥵 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: If it is a response to how you look, they are telling you they find you very attractive. It is flirtatious and physical. If the conversation is about weather, exercise or food, it only means they are hot or worn out.

Very often, yes. It is one of the most direct ways to call someone hot without typing the word. It is not exclusively flirty, though; people use it all summer long for nothing more than high temperatures.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🥵 and 🔥?
faqs.a: 🔥 praises almost anything: a song, an outfit, a play. 🥵 is a bodily reaction, so when it is a compliment it is specifically about physical attraction. Calling a new album 🔥 is normal; calling it 🥵 would be odd.

faqs.q: When was the hot face emoji added?
faqs.a: It came with Unicode 11.0 in 2018, in the same release as its opposite, the blue cold face, and also the woozy face, the partying face and the pleading face.
